ai.description: *Tylototriton panwaensis* reaches 60–70 mm. It is dark brown with orange markings on the head, vertebral ridge, and rib nodules. It features a distinct, flattened head and prominent dorsolateral warts.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Tylototriton panwaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and elevated dorsolateral bony ridge that connects the head to the tail base.
ai.habitat: *Tylototriton panwaensis* inhabits high-altitude evergreen broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found near small, stagnant pools at elevations above 2,000m.
ai.behavior: *Tylototriton panwaensis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Tylototriton panwaensis* breeds in ponds during the monsoon (May–July), laying small clutches of eggs individually attached to submerged vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Tylototriton panwaensis* is found in the high-altitude forests of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically occurring at elevations between 1,800 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: *Tylototriton panwaensis* emits a low-pitched, pulsed call consisting of short, rhythmic notes, typically heard from males breeding in shallow, forested mountain pools.
